title: Personal Exercise Programme
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Personal Exercise Programme in GCSE PE.
meta_desc: GCSE PE adventure on Personal Exercise Programme.
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Personal Exercise Programme.

concepts.def: A structured training plan built around an individual's goals, current fitness and chosen activity, applying the principles of training over a set period.
A framework for planning training that adjusts Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type to ensure improvement and avoid plateaus.
Gradually increasing the demands placed on the body during training so that fitness keeps improving without causing injury.
The principle that training should match the demands of the chosen activity, working the relevant muscles, energy systems and skills.
The principle that fitness gains are lost when training stops or intensity drops, so improvements decline if a programme is not maintained.
The rest the body needs between training sessions to adapt and repair, preventing overtraining and reducing the risk of injury.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Personal Exercise Programme — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Personal Exercise Programme brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Personal Exercise Programme.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What do the letters FITT stand for?
options: Fitness, Intensity, Time, Type
Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type
Frequency, Injury, Time, Training
Force, Intensity, Tempo, Type
Training the same way every week
Gradually increasing training demands over time
Resting for the whole programme
Only training one muscle
Be random
Match the demands of your activity
Avoid the main muscles used
Use only one exercise

mcqs.q: Reversibility describes what happens when you:
options: Train harder
Stop training and lose fitness
Eat a balanced diet
Warm up properly

mcqs.q: If you stop training, what happens to your fitness gains?
options: So you only ever do cardio.
They stay the same permanently.
They reverse and decline (reversibility).
They keep improving on their own.
So you only ever do cardio.
Training as hard as possible in every single session.
Gradually increasing the training demands over time.
Keeping the workload exactly the same each week.

mcqs.q: Why must a PEP follow the specificity principle?
options: So every athlete does the identical programme.
They keep improving on their own.
So you only ever do cardio.
So training matches the muscles and energy systems the activity actually uses.
